sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Burien?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Burien means selling in a King County suburb of 51,859 people (Census Bureau estimate, July 1, 2025) that sits on Puget Sound just south of Seattle and west of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

Gottlieb Burian settled beside what is now Lake Burien in 1884, and the area grew from a trail-served community into a suburb. Voters incorporated the city on February 28, 1993, partly because residents wanted a local voice on the airport's planned third runway. A 2010 annexation of the southern part of North Highline, with 14,292 residents, lifted the population past 52,000 and made Burien the 25th largest city in the state. Burien covers 11.19 square miles, including 5.5 miles of Puget Sound shoreline.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Burien homes?
sections.html:
More than half of Burien households own their home, and the median value is $638,800. About 34 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, and the city publishes its renting handbook in English and Spanish.

sections.h2: Which parts of Burien shape a house's appeal?
sections.html:
Burien borders Seattle and the unincorporated communities of White Center and Boulevard Park on the north, Tukwila and SeaTac on the east, and Normandy Park on the south. Where a house sits within that frame affects how buyers describe it.

  • Olde Burien surrounds Southwest 152nd Street on the west side of Ambaum Boulevard, and Town Square, completed in 2017, holds shops, condominiums, apartments, a senior living center, a King County library branch and City Hall.
  • Ambaum Boulevard follows the old Lake Burien Railway route, which opened in 1915 and carried a small passenger train to Seattle.
  • Lake Burien is a state-owned water body ringed by private property with no public access, which makes lakefront views and access a point to describe carefully.
  • Three Tree Point, just west of town, drew Seattle visitors to sunbathe and swim in the early 1900s.

The Highline School District serves Burien, with Highline High School, Big Picture, CHOICE Academy and the Puget Sound Skills Center. Confirm the school assignment for the address before you quote it in a listing.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit help sell a Burien house?
sections.html: Burien sits at the junction of State Routes 509 and 518, immediately northwest of the airport, and Ambaum Boulevard and Des Moines Memorial Drive carry traffic to the north. King County Metro and Sound Transit run buses from the Burien Transit Center, which opened in June 2009, to Seattle, Bellevue, the airport, West Seattle, Kent, Auburn, Renton, Des Moines and Tukwila. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute at 26.7 minutes. Buyers who work near the airport or downtown Seattle will weigh that against the price, so lead with the transit and freeway access when you describe the house.

sections.h2: Which Burien rental rules apply when you sell a house with tenants?
sections.html:
Burien's rental rules affect a seller whose house has a renter in it. The city requires an annual rental housing business license, handled by the state Business Licensing Service, but single-family residences, condos, townhomes, manufactured homes and accessory dwelling units are exempt. For other rentals, the 2026 fee per complex is $323.80 for 1 to 10 units, $809.50 for 11 to 50 units and $971.41 for 51 or more.

  • Under the Rental Housing Policy in BMC 5.63, a landlord needs one of a list of just causes to evict, and wanting to sell the unit counts only after the tenant gets at least 90 days' written notice.
  • A landlord cannot evict from a unit that lacks a required license, or whose required inspection was not finished by the deadline.
  • The inspection program, in place since 2021, requires at least 20 percent of covered units to be inspected every three years.
  • Owners of buildings with five or more units that rent at affordable levels must give the city 60 calendar days' written notice before listing the building for sale.

State law also limits rent increases (RCW 59.18.700 and 59.18.720). The city's rental housing program answers questions at (206) 241-4647.

sections.h2: What does a Burien seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
Real estate excise tax falls on the seller. At the Census median value of $638,800, the state portion under RCW 82.45.060 works out to $7,232: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 comes to $5,775, and 1.28 percent on the remaining $113,800 comes to $1,457. The Department of Revenue says the local portion must be added, and the county treasurer collects it with the affidavit. For sales starting January 1, 2027, the break points rise to of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

Washington also requires a seller of improved residential property to deliver a completed disclosure statement within five business days after the contract is mutually accepted, unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind (RCW 64.06.020). The form covers title, water, structural items, systems and fixtures and environmental questions, so gather permits and repair records before you start.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a Burien house?
sections.html: State law sets the dates. First-half taxes are due on or before April 30 and second-half taxes on or before October 31, under RCW 84.56.020. Residential property with four or fewer units picks up nine percent annual interest when it is delinquent, and the statute allows no penalties on that class of property. Ask King County Treasury Operations for the current amount and any balance due before you list. Each tax statement must also describe the senior and disabled exemption (RCW 84.36.379 through 84.36.389) and the deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Burien house quickly?
sections.html:
A seller with a tight timeline, a tenant in place or a house that needs work usually compares three routes.

  • List with an agent, which suits a vacant house in good condition.
  • Sell it yourself and complete the disclosure form and the excise tax affidavit without an agent.
  • Ask for a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is, which can help when repairs, an inherited house or a tenant's notice period stand in the way.

Whatever you pick, check the notice rules in BMC 5.63 before you ask a tenant to leave, and keep the 90 day notice period in the schedule.

faqs.q: Does a Burien single-family rental need the city rental housing license?
faqs.a: No. Burien exempts single-family residences, condominiums, townhomes, manufactured homes and accessory dwelling units from the annual rental housing business license. Other eviction and notice rules in BMC 5.63 can still apply.

faqs.q: Can I end a tenancy in Burien because I am selling the house?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with at least 90 days' written notice, because selling the unit is one of the just causes in BMC 5.63.070. Without a valid cause, the city rules do not allow the eviction.

faqs.q: How much is the state excise tax on a $638,800 Burien sale?
faqs.a: The state portion is about $7,232, which is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 plus 1.28 percent on the remaining $113,800. The local portion is added on top.

faqs.q: What must a Burien seller give the buyer?
faqs.a: A completed seller disclosure statement, delivered within five business days after both sides accept the contract, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Burien?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. Delinquent residential tax with four or fewer units carries nine percent annual interest.
